messages.subject: Re: Renjin & icCube
parts:
Great,
You won't need devSVG or most of the graphics "devices" for R, Renjin's (incomplete) implementation writes to the standard Graphics2D API, so you can use any jvm-based graphics library that supports this API, for example batik (http://xmlgraphics.apache.org/batik/) for SVG, the standard java renderers for PNG, JPEG, etc, or the GraphicsIO library in the FreeHep project (http://java.freehep.or

But again, Renjin's base graphics implementation is incomplete, so it will take a bit of work to get say, ggplot2 working on Renjin. Take a look at the awtIntegrationTest() :

http://code.google.com/p/renjin/source/browse/trunk/core/src/test/java/org/renjin/primitives/graphics/GraphicsTest.java#79

for a starting point

Alex
